ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7), and refer the driver's account to Ryde review for a false arrival confirmation + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
This is a no-show (waiting/cancellation fee) dispute under RydeX, cancelled by the driver [F3], so it enters through NS-0 and is tested against NS-1. The $6.61 fee on the fare record is the single published cancellation fee and no surge applied [F6][F7], so the quantum is not in issue; the question is whether NS-1's conditions for charging it are met [NS-0][FARE-1].

NS-1 requires (i) an arrival indication, (ii) that at the moment of the "I'm Here" tap the driver was at the pickup point, and (iii) more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting there until cancellation. The GPS record settles all three: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 12:06:15 while 600 m from the pickup [F5], his closest approach over the whole window was 599 m at 12:06:55 [F1], he stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap [F5], and he was stationary 600 m away from 12:05:55 to 12:09:25 [F2]. The timeline confirms the platform never recorded him at the pickup at all (driver_arrived_at null) [F4]. So conditions (ii) and (iii) fail [NS-1].

The driver's statement that he "pressed I'm Here and waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12] is a statement contradicted by the gps and timeline records and must give way; the timing rule is settled, not open. His 12:06 chat message "I'm here already" [F8] is likewise a location claim the system record does not support, while the rider's 12:07 message "I'm at the pickup point, no car here. Where are you?" [F9] is consistent with the car being 600 m away [F1]. The record does not require the rider's presence to be independently proved: NS-1 places the burden of the (i)–(iii) conditions on the driver, and all of them must hold for the fee to stand.

Because NS-1 (i)-(iii) are not all satisfied, the consequence in NS-2 follows: the $6.61 is refunded in full, and where the driver tapped "I'm Here" while GPS placed him outside the pickup radius, an account referral is added [NS-2][F5][F1]. No traffic or weather cause explains the position 600 m away — no incidents on the route, only a 20–29 km/h band on Jalan Besar, fair weather 0.0 mm rain [F14][F13][F15] — so nothing under RD-4 rescues the driver's position. The refund is issued as a Ryde voucher per NS-7 and Ryde retains final discretion on refunds [NS-7].

Safety screen: I read all three chat messages [F8][F9][F10], the driver's written statement [F12] and the complaint. They contain a pickup arrangement, a request for the car's location, a cancellation notice and a factual account — no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none [SAFE-1].

Amount: the disputed item is the cancellation fee recorded on the fare record, $6.61 [F6][F3][NS-2]; refund_full.

rejected_claims.reason: The 3 min 30 s stationary period ran 12:05:55–12:09:25 at 600 m from the pickup, not at it, and the driver stayed within 200 m for 0 s after the tap [F2][F5]; NS-1 (iii) requires the continuous wait to be at the pickup after the arrival confirmation, so duration alone does not satisfy it.

Tapping the button is NS-1 (i) only; the tap at 12:06:15 was made 600 m from the pickup and the platform never recorded him at the pickup [F5][F4], so NS-1 (ii) fails despite the tap and the 12:06 message [F8].

The rider's 12:07 message is consistent with the GPS record that the car was 600 m away [F9][F1]; a rider statement of position is confirmed rather than contradicted by the system record, and no rider no-show can be built on the driver's unsupported 'I'm here already' [F8] under NS-1.

The quantum $6.61 with 1.0x surge is not disputed [F6][F7], but under NS-0 the fee is chargeable only if NS-1's conditions are met, and they are not [F5][F1][F4]; a correctly quantified fee is still not chargeable.

Profile facts cannot decide the case and may only support an added action [F17]; RD-6's flag limb is not triggered as a repetition basis here, and the driver's history does not cure the NS-1 (ii)/(iii) failures [F5][F1].

The complete timestamped chat record [F11] is why the contradiction resolves against the driver: the chat asserts presence at the pickup [F8] while the gps/timeline record shows he never was there [F1][F4][F5], and NS-1 places the arrival conditions on the driver.

actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the arrival confirmation; (iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.
